leads.locality: 'parc municipal Blanchoud', stated 5th arrondissement, Lyon; exact location not found
leads.reason: 2026-08-20 pass: found via the guichetdusavoir.org library Q&A service (fetched directly, not from a search summary), which quotes the booklet 'Arbres remarquables du Rhone' (2000): 'Le cedre du Liban dans le parc municipal Blanchoud dans le 5e : plus de 30 metres de haut et 6,50 m de circonference (page 44).' That is one real source with a specific citation, but a park called 'Blanchoud' could not be located under that name in any current map, Ville de Lyon page or ruesdelyon.net listing searched this pass. CAUTION: a WebSearch AI summary conflated this tree with the already-published lyo_006 (Atlas Cedar of Parc de la Chapelle, 9th arrondissement, a Cedrus atlantica, not Cedrus libani), inventing a 'Blanchoud/Sabattier house' bicentennial cedar with lyo_006's own measurements (28m, 32m crown, 635cm). That invented merge was discarded; do not repeat it. The Parc de la Chapelle grounds (18 rue de la Chapelle, formerly the Sabatier property, per ruesdelyon.net fetched directly) are a distinct, already-published park with a real 6.75m-circumference Atlas cedar of its own, unrelated to this lead. Needs someone to identify the actual 'parc Blanchoud', possibly a renamed or absorbed 5th-arrondissement park, before this can be pinned or even confirmed as still standing; no age was estimated because a park could not be confirmed, let alone a coordinate.
